title: Platform systems & services: how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospective and roadmap (Q3 2026)
author: Samantha Lee
content:
Summary
-------
This document collects the canonical platform systems & services guidance for the Platform team: systems inventory, standard how-tos for common operational tasks, dashboard and alert definitions, post-incident retrospectives from Q2-Q3 2026, and the roadmap for the next two quarters. It is intended as the single-page entry for on-call engineers, service owners, and technical program managers.

Scope
-----
Applies to the Platform Systems & Services ownership area (service catalog: routing, ingress, service-discovery, feature-flag-service, job-scheduler, config-store) and to runbooks maintained by the Platform team. This document complements per-service runbooks under /confluence/eng-platform/*runbooks.

Systems and Services Inventory (high level)
-----------------------------------------
- routing-service (k8s, NGINX-based edge, GKE prod clusters) - responsible for traffic shaping and canary routing. Owner: platform-routing.
- platform-api (k8s microservice) - control-plane APIs used by Redwood Console. Owner: platform-api.
- config-store (etcd v3.6, HA cluster) - global configuration and feature flags. Owner: platform-config.
- job-scheduler (Temporal) - background job orchestration and retries. Owner: platform-scheduler.
- cache-service (redis-cluster, 6.x, clustered) - prefix/KV cache used by serving runtime. Owner: platform-cache.
- metrics-ingest (Prometheus remote_write + Cortex) - central metrics pipeline. Owner: observability-team.
- log-aggregation (Loki + Fluentd) - centralized logs. Owner: observability-team.
- alert-router (Alertmanager backed by PagerDuty) - routes alerts to on-call. Owner: eng-sre.

Service SLOs and target thresholds (summary)
-------------------------------------------
- routing-service: p99 request latency < 45ms, availability 99.95% monthly.
- platform-api: p95 < 250ms, availability 99.9%.
- config-store: write latency p99 < 30ms, availability 99.99% (etcd quorum).
- job-scheduler: job success rate >= 99.5% over 24h window.
- cache-service: cache hit rate >= 80% for prefix cache, eviction rate < 1%/minute.

How-tos (common operational tasks)
----------------------------------
1) Emergency config rollback (config-store)
   - When to use: a config change causes systemic failures (errors across services or cascading retries).
   - Steps:
     1. Open the config-store UI: https://config.redwood.internal or use CLI.
     2. Identify offending change: use recent_history --since 1h (example):
        curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/changes?since=1h"
     3. Roll back to prior version:
        curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"action":"rollback","key":"feature/kv-prefix","version":123}' https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/changes
     4. Verify downstream health: check platform-api and routing-service dashboards (see Dashboard links below).
     5. Notify #platform-ops and update incident ticket with params.

2) Forcing a job-scheduler (Temporal) retry for critical processing pipeline
   - CLI snippet to query failed workflows older than 30m:
     tctl --ns redwood workflow list --query "CloseTime < now() - 30m and Status = 'FAILED'"
   - To retry a single workflow: tctl workflow reset --workflow-id <id> --reason "manual-retry-after-fix"
   - Ownership: platform-scheduler on-call to approve escalations beyond 5 retries.

3) Replacing a Redis shard (cache-service)
   - Pre-checks: confirm replication lag < 100ms, current eviction rate < 0.5%/min.
   - Steps (high level):
     1. Provision new node via terraform module: module.redis_shard.apply(shard_id=X).
     2. Add to cluster, wait for slot migration, monitor cluster health: redis-cli -c CLUSTER INFO.
     3. Remove old node after slot migration completes and client health is green.
   - Post-check: run integration test suite: ./scripts/integration-tests --cache-checks

Dashboards & Alerts (operational definitions)
--------------------------------------------
Canonical dashboards (links)
- Platform Overview: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/PLATFORM/overview\- routing-service: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ROUTING/routing-service\- platform-api: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/API/platform-api\- config-store (etcd): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ETCD/etcd-cluster\- cache-service: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CACHE/cache-service

Key alerts and firing conditions (Alertmanager -> pager duty)
- routing_service_high_error_rate
  - Expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-service",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-service"}[5m])) > 0.02
  - For: 2m
  - Severity: page
  - Runbook: follow 'Routing-service 5xx surge' runbook below.

- platform_api_latency_p95
  - Expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"platform-api.*"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25
  - For: 5m
  - Severity: page (if duration > 10m then escalate to infra lead)

- etcd_quorum_loss
  - Expr: etcd_server_has_leader == 0 or etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total > 2
  - For: 1m
  - Severity: page
  - Runbook: immediate paging, do not attempt unilateral restart without {platform-config} approval.

Alert routing policy briefly
- SEV:page -> PagerDuty P0 / on-call platform engineer (15m SLA).
- SEV:ticket -> Slack alert to #platform-ops + ticket auto-created in JIRA (SLA 24h).

Runbooks (excerpts)
-------------------
Routing-service 5xx surge (excerpt)
1. Triage: open routing dashboard, time range last 15m, group by upstream cluster.
2. If errors from a single upstream: mark upstream unhealthy in routing UI (temporary blacklist) and notify upstream owner.
3. If errors across many upstreams: check config-store for recent changes; revert if applicable (see Emergency config rollback).
4. If traffic surge is legitimate, consider increasing capacity via autoscaler: kubectl scale deploy routing-service --replicas=<n> (check HPA first).
5. Post-incident: add a postmortem link to incident ticket and tag the incident with root cause.

Etcd quorum-loss (excerpt)
1. Do not restart etcd processes in isolation.
2. Verify network connectivity across the three nodes: sudo iptables -L; nc -vz <peer_ip> 2379
3. If a node is unreachable for > 2m, remove it from the cluster using `etcdctl member remove <id>` only after coordination with platform-config lead.
4. If quorum cannot be recovered, follow escalate-to-oncall-sre -> exec runbook to restore from backup (see below).

Incident retrospective highlights (Q2-Q3 2026)
----------------------------------------------
- Incident: 2026-06-12 platform-api regression caused by a config rollout. Impact: console errors for ~18 minutes, increased API latency for 35 minutes.
  - Root cause: missing defensive null-check in config merge code + config-store allowed rapid multi-key rollouts without staged canary.
  - Actions taken: immediate rollback, added server-side defensive checks, introduced staged rollout feature to config-store.
  - Follow-ups (completed): canary rollout UI, preflight validation for critical config keys.

- Incident: 2026-08-04 redis shard eviction due to memory misconfiguration after autoscaling event. Impact: degraded cache hit rate -> increased token cost for serving runtime.
  - Root cause: new autoscaler profile for low-memory instance type not compatible with redis maxmemory policy.
  - Actions: revert autoscaler profile, add eviction threshold alert, update terraform default instance type.

Retrospective takeaways
- Improve preflight test coverage for config rollouts (integration tests must run against a staging config-store with representative keys).
- Add synthetic end-to-end checks that validate platform-api and routing-service at 1-min cadence.
- Create a standardized postmortem template and require action items with owners and dates.

Roadmap (Q4 2026 - Q1 2027)
---------------------------
Planned projects and milestones:
- Q4 2026: Config-store staged rollouts (GA), automated preflight validations, and canary web UI (owner: platform-config).
- Q4 2026: Dashboard consolidation - merge per-service dashboards into a Platform Overview panel with alert correlation (owner: observability).
- Q1 2027: Runbook automation pilot - integrate Alertmanager webhook with runbook-runner to post suggested runbook steps into Slack thread (owner: eng-sre / platform-ops).
- Q1 2027: Cache autoscaling improvements - add adaptive eviction thresholds and cross-region replication tests (owner: platform-cache).

Planned deprecations
- Remove legacy statsd pipeline in favor of Prometheus remote_write by end of Q1 2027.

Ownership & escalation matrix
-----------------------------
- First responder: service owner on-call (listed in each service runbook).
- On-call escalation: platform on-call -> eng-sre -> platform lead -> CTO for incidents > 4 hours or customer-impacting outages.
- Contact points: PagerDuty, #platform-ops Slack, incident-jira template at https://jira.redwood.internal/secure/CreateIssue.jspa

Appendix A - Example Prometheus alert rule (YAML snippet)
--------------------------------------------------------
groups:
- name: platform_alerts
  rules:
  - alert: routing_service_high_error_rate
    expr: |
      sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-service",status=~"5.."}[5m]))
      / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="routing-service"}[5m])) > 0.02
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "Routing service 5xx rate > 2%"
      runbook: "https://confluence.redwood.internal/confluence/eng-platform/routing-service-5xx-surge-runbook"

Appendix B - Runbook & doc hygiene guidelines
----------------------------------------------
- All runbooks must include: Summary, Trigger (alerts/conditions), Pager list, Step-by-step remediation, Verification steps, Postmortem link template.
- Keep runbooks short: fewer than 30 steps for critical pages.
- Ownership: each runbook must list a primary owner and secondary reviewer and must be reviewed at least quarterly.

Appendix C - Quick CLI snippets
-------------------------------
- View last 30m of platform-api p95 in Prometheus using promtool curl endpoint:
  curl -G "https://prometheus.redwood.internal/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"platform-api.*"}[5m])) by (le))' --data-urlencode 'time='`date -u +%s`

- Trigger a config-store preflight manually:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"action":"preflight","keys":["feature/kv-prefix"]}' \
    https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/preflight
